# AI assistance disclosure

Disclose meaningful AI assistance in each affected issue and PR, including generated code, designs, documentation, debugging and tests. Use `None` if no meaningful assistance occurred. Do not infer or retroactively attribute historical work to AI.

```text
AI Assistance:
- Tool:
- Purpose:
- Human contribution:
- Verification performed:
```

Recommended commit footer:

```text
AI-Assisted: Codex used for <purpose>; reviewed and verified by <contributor>.
```

Replace placeholders with facts. Do not claim human review until it happens. Contributors remain responsible for correctness, originality, security and understanding the work. Never send secrets, confidential agreements or unapproved stakeholder data to AI tools. Summarize assistance in iteration and release records.

## Declaration levels

Every source file and every feature or fix pull request states one of: **No substantial AI-generated code**, **Below 50% AI-generated**, **50% or more AI-generated**. Code first generated by AI still counts as AI-generated after a student edits it. Run `python3 scripts/check_ai_declarations.py` to list files without a declaration.

## Issue #27 run telemetry

Tool: Claude Code. Assisted with the run recorder, interrupted-run recovery,
log redaction, run status/detail APIs and their tests
([PR #74](https://github.com/ham340i/Industrial-Data-Pipelinen-Platform/pull/74)).
Verified by 30 automated tests ([record](../docs/testing/issue-27-run-telemetry.md)).
Correction found in review: two failure logs included full exception text,
which could leak bound SQL values, and were reduced to the exception type.

Further corrections found in `ham340i`'s review of
[PR #74](https://github.com/ham340i/Industrial-Data-Pipelinen-Platform/pull/74)
(Claude Code, verified by new/updated automated tests, one per item):
the `0002` migration dropped and recreated `runs` via a batch CHECK-constraint
add, which fails with a foreign-key error on any workspace that already has
artifact rows referencing a run; changed to plain `ADD COLUMN`/`DROP COLUMN`
(no table rebuild) and moved the `duration_ms >= 0` invariant from a DB CHECK
constraint to an ORM `@validates` method. The credential redactor's
key/value regex missed JSON-quoted keys (`"password": "..."`) entirely and
truncated quoted multi-word values at the first space; both are now matched
and replaced in full. It also only redacted backslash-style Windows paths,
missing forward-slash absolute paths (`C:/Users/...`); the path rule now
matches both separators. The run/block row-count recorder collapsed "no
tabular data was measured" (e.g. a trigger emitting only a `ControlSignal`)
into a reported `0`, indistinguishable from a genuinely empty table; it now
preserves `None` for unmeasured counts while keeping the separate, intentional
convention that a block with no input edges at all reports `rows_in=0`.

A follow-up review on the same PR found the redaction fix above was still
incomplete: its quoted-value regex excluded both quote characters
universally (`[^"']`) instead of only the matching delimiter, so a credential
containing the *other* quote character, or an escaped matching quote, either
skipped the redaction rule entirely or had the match end early and leak the
remainder - confirmed persisted in `Run`/`RunBlock.error_reason` and returned
from `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}`. Replaced with a delimiter-specific,
escape-aware pattern (`"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"` / the single-quote equivalent) and
added regression tests covering both quote types, escaped quotes, and the
persistence/API path directly, not just the redactor unit.

A second follow-up found the JSON/dict-style rule still only matched when
the dictionary key and value used the *same* quote style (e.g.
`{"password": "secret"}` or `{'password': 'secret'}`); a mixed pair like
`{"password": 'secret'}` matched neither that rule nor the bare key=value
rule, so the value passed through completely unredacted - again confirmed
persisted and returned from the API. The key's quote style is now matched
independently of the value's, and a regression test was added for both
mixed-style orderings.

## Issue #29 Manual and Timer triggers, execute API

AI contribution: below 50%.
Tool: Claude Code. Assisted with the Manual/Timer trigger block contracts,
the execute and timer start/stop/status APIs, the single-process no-overlap
interval scheduler, and their tests
([design](../docs/architecture/triggers-and-execute.md),
[verification](../docs/testing/issue-29-triggers-and-execute.md)).
Verified by 24 new automated tests (702 passing overall), run twice to rule
out timing flakiness, plus manual smoke tests of every execute/timer HTTP
path against a real SQLite database before the automated tests were written.

Two mistakes were caught and corrected during development, not after:
a `zip(..., strict=True)` in a test helper's deliberately length-offset
pairwise comparison always raised (fixed to `strict=False`), and an initial
assumption that stopping a timer mid-execution would mark a single-block run
`cancelled` was wrong - cooperative cancellation cannot preempt a block
already running, so it finishes and is correctly recorded as `succeeded`.
The test and the design doc were corrected to document the real behavior.

`adamoug`'s review of [PR #76](https://github.com/ham340i/Industrial-Data-Pipelinen-Platform/pull/76)
found four real concurrency gaps in the stop/shutdown path, all confirmed
and fixed, not argued with: a timed-out `stop()` returned as if the timer
were gone while its thread could still be running; that same timed-out
`stop()` left the pipeline id free for a replacement timer to start
concurrently with the old thread's still-finishing block; the loop's
stop-check and `stop()`'s own signal/cancel step used separate locks,
leaving a window where a tick could start at the exact instant `stop()`
ran; and `stop_all()` (used right before the app closes the database at
shutdown) had the same bounded-join gap, so a slow block could still be
running under a database the shutdown path had already closed. Fixed by
having `stop()` report whether the thread actually exited (raising a new
`TimerStopTimedOut`, mapped to a structured 409, instead of lying), keeping
a timed-out timer registered until it truly exits, merging the stop-check
and signal/cancel onto one lock, and making `stop_all()` fall back to an
unbounded join so it never returns early. See
[the updated verification record](../docs/testing/issue-29-triggers-and-execute.md)
for the four regression tests, including a deterministic one that drives
the exact lock race instead of relying on timing.

## Issue #37 API/engine block integration matrix

AI contribution: 50% or more AI-generated overall, declared per file exactly
as in the PR description: `50% or more` for `tests/integration_support.py`,
`tests/test_integration_matrix.py`, `tests/test_integration_failures.py`,
`tests/test_integration_contracts.py`, `tests/fixtures/contracts/*.json`,
`frontend/src/api/contracts.test.ts`,
`docs/testing/issue-37-integration-matrix.md` and
`docs/individual-contributions/menaboulus-iteration-4.md`; `below 50%` for
the small edits to `app/artifacts/api.py`, `app/blocks/files.py`,
`app/workspace.py`, `app/pipelines/api.py`, `app/preview/service.py`,
`app/runs/scheduler.py`, `tests/test_artifact_api.py`, `tests/conftest.py`,
`frontend/vite.config.ts` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
Tool: Claude Code. Assisted with the API-level integration fixtures
(`tests/integration_support.py`), the source → transform → quality → sink
compatibility matrix, the malformed-definition / schema-mismatch /
timeout-response cases, the shared response fixtures parsed by the frontend
(`tests/test_integration_contracts.py`, `frontend/src/api/contracts.test.ts`),
the two compatibility fixes below, the CI JUnit capture, and the
documentation. Verified by 39 new backend tests (880 passing overall), 4
frontend parser tests, Ruff, mypy, ESLint, Prettier and `tsc`
([record](../docs/testing/issue-37-integration-matrix.md)). Pull request:
[PR #85](https://github.com/ham340i/Industrial-Data-Pipelinen-Platform/pull/85); independent review by the planned student reviewer `Al-Yousef`
is requested and pending.

Problems found and corrected: the artifact query endpoint resolved Parquet
files beneath the bare workspace root while the execute API publishes them
under `<root>/<project id>/`, so every artifact from a real run was reported
unavailable; fixed in `app/artifacts/api.py` and pinned by the Parquet matrix
cases. File sinks writing into a not-yet-existing `outputs/` folder failed
with a misleading `write_failed`; the sink now creates the folder inside the
already-checked project path, pinned by a regression test. Three mistakes in
the generated tests themselves were caught by running them and corrected
without touching the product: re-running a no-clobber sink, reusing a
pipeline name within a project, and a leak assertion that tripped on an
ordinary `/` in an error message.

Corrections found in `Al-Yousef`'s review of
[PR #85](https://github.com/ham340i/Industrial-Data-Pipelinen-Platform/pull/85)
(Claude Code, each verified by a new automated test): the project-scoped
artifact query handed `<workspace>/<project id>` to `resource_path`, which
resolves and then trusts the root it is given, so a symlink or junction
installed at the project folder redirected the query into another project's
folder (project A's metadata with project B's rows) or outside the workspace
entirely. The execute and timer paths built the same unchecked folder. One
shared rule, `project_data_folder` in `app/workspace.py`, now rejects a
missing or aliased project folder; the artifact query answers
`409 artifact_unavailable`, execute refuses with `422
workspace_project_folder` before creating a run, timer ticks fall back to
running without a workspace so the failure is recorded, and the preview
service reuses the rule instead of its own copy. Second, the
backend/frontend contract bridge compared only JSON types, so a same-type
incompatible change such as `level: "warn"` passed the backend check while
the Builder parser rejected it; the bridge now also applies the parser's
own value rules (enumerations, identifier format, event ordering, the
`valid`/diagnostics relationship) to every live response and to the recorded
fixtures, with same-type negative cases on both sides. Third, the AI
declaration above was restated per file to match the PR description.

A second Codex-assisted re-review of PR #85 (at `48adc20`) found that the
listing-based project lookup compared names byte for byte, so a case-only
rename of the project folder on NTFS or default APFS, where the original
path still addresses the same directory, turned preview and execute into
`422`, artifact queries into `409` and scheduled runs into
`workspace_required` failures. The lookup now follows the filesystem's own
case rule, probed with listing-derived names only. It also found the
contract bridge accepted a `limit: 21` echo, a well-formed UUID for another
project in a list item and a different run id in a detail response, which
the Builder's guards reject; the rules are now bound to the requested ids
and fixed pagination, with negative cases for each reproduction. Both
corrections by Claude Code, each verified by a new automated test.

## Release 1 readiness refactor and documentation (#36)

Tool: Claude Code, directed by ham340i. AI contribution: 50% or more AI-generated.

What it did: split `app/blocks/files.py`, `file_preview.py` and `transforms.py` into smaller modules; extracted helpers so that no backend file exceeds 500 lines, no function exceeds 50 lines and none exceeds cyclomatic complexity 15; added central logging configuration and request logging; replaced silently ignored exceptions with log statements; moved test-only dependencies out of the runtime manifest; extended Dependabot; rewrote the README, the Wiki sources, the Release 1 notes and the remaining-actions list from repository and GitHub data.

AI-assisted files: `app/blocks/resources.py`, `sinks.py`, `csv_preview.py`, `inference.py`, `relational.py`, `parquet_preview.py`, `file_preview.py`, `files.py`, `transforms.py`, `base.py`, `quality.py`, `sql.py`, `tabular.py`, `context.py`, `app/pipelines/validation.py`, `app/execution/runtime.py`, `app/preview/service.py`, `app/preview/api.py`, `app/artifacts/query.py`, `app/sources/sql.py`, `app/workspace.py`, `app/main.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/logging_config.py`, `tests/test_logging_config.py`, `scripts/check_repository.py`, `scripts/check_release_plan.py`, `scripts/check_ai_declarations.py`.

Verification: the refactor changed structure, not behaviour. The existing 913 backend tests passed unchanged apart from import paths, four logging tests were added (917 pass), and Ruff, Ruff format and mypy strict are clean. Frontend code was not changed.

Problems found and corrected during the work: an automatic unused-import fix removed `typing` imports that a moved class still needed, caught by mypy and restored; the first logging configuration disabled propagation and broke an existing telemetry test that captures log records, so propagation was kept on; a repository-tool test pinned the exact contents of `.env.example` and was updated for the new non-secret `LPS_LOG_LEVEL` default.

Not verified: no human review has taken place yet. The documentation states facts taken from the repository and the GitHub API on November 17, 2026; judgements in the retrospective are observations for the team to confirm.

## Source-file declarations added at Release 1

At Release 1 only 58 of 201 source files carried a declaration. Claude Code added 104 more, using evidence only, never a guess:

1. For each undeclared file, `git log --first-parent -m` on `main` listed every merged pull request that changed it.
2. Each of those pull requests' own "AI Assistance" section was read. Pull requests #3, #39, #43, #46, #47, #59, #61, #62, #63, #64, #66, #67, #69, #70, #71, #77, #81, #82 and #83 state that an AI tool generated the implementation, tests or tooling.
3. A file received `50% or more AI-generated` only when every pull request that changed it is in that list. Repository scripts committed directly to `main` before pull requests were used are covered by the "This repository foundation" entry above.
4. `app/blocks/relational.py` holds the Join and Aggregate logic from #72, whose author reports AI help only with tests, documentation and formatting; it is declared `below 50% AI-generated` even though Claude Code restructured it.
5. Files changed by #44, #48, #51, #52, #65 or #72 were left undeclared, because those pull requests do not say how much code AI generated. Their authors must declare them.

Authors who find a declaration wrong for their file should correct it; the pull request record is the evidence used, not the final word.
